art.subject: Common Swift (Apus apus), adult of the eastern race pekinensis, in late spring: uniformly dark sooty brown, a little paler and browner than western birds, with a clear whitish throat patch that is larger in this race; wings blackish brown, the inner flight feathers slightly paler in good light; rump dark, the same colour as the back; underparts uniform dark brown with no pale scaling. Tiny black bill; dark eye; tiny feathered feet hidden in flight.
art.pose: in fast flight high over a ridge, wings swept back like a sickle, seen from slightly below
art.scene: Korean coastal hills under a wide late-spring sky in May; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Swift a little larger than a Barn Swallow but with much longer wings; about the size of the Pacific Swift, with a shorter, less deeply forked tail. Slim, torpedo-shaped body, short broad head with no visible neck, tiny bill with a wide gape. Wings very long, narrow and scythe-shaped, swept back from a short arm. Tail of medium length with a shallow fork, often closed to a point. Legs tiny and almost never seen; it never perches on wires or twigs. Flight fast, with flickering wingbeats and long glides.
avoid: Do not paint a white rump band or pale scaling on the underparts; these mark the Pacific Swift (Apus pacificus), the common swift in Korea.
Do not paint it like a swallow: no white or orange underparts, no long tail streamers, no perching on a wire.
Do not give it a deeply forked tail; the fork is shallow.
Do not show visible legs or a large bill.
